evals.prompt: In this folder are SVG exports of my app's screens from Figma, with live text and layer names. My product is Planloom, project management for small teams. Turn the screens into a Product film of 20 to 45 seconds: 1920x1080 at 60 fps, as an MP4 with sound. Show what the app does screen by screen, add a few short headlines, and end on the product's name. Animate the real layers found by their names so after a design change I can export again and render again with one command. Make the sound in code from the same timeline. Draw every frame from its time stamp in a headless browser and encode it with ffmpeg.
evals.expected_output: An MP4 at exactly 1920x1080/60fps in the 20-45s range with a synthesised audio track; a single re-run command; layers targeted by their Figma names rather than coordinates; the source SVGs byte-identical afterwards; frames verified reproducible.
files: three Figma SVG exports with live <text> and named layers

evals.prompt: Here are four screens exported from Sketch. Can you make a 30 second launch video out of them? I want it to feel premium - not just screenshots fading into each other.
evals.expected_output: Checks the export first and reports what it found. Builds a film using camera and layer moves (3D tilt, vector zoom, lifting a layer out of its window) rather than crossfades, with sound. Asks before installing anything.

evals.prompt: I exported our dashboard from Figma but I ticked 'outline text'. Can you still animate it into a product video?
evals.expected_output: Detects that the text is outlined into paths, says so before starting, explains which beats become impossible (typing, counters, streamed text), and asks for a re-export with live text rather than quietly building a degraded film.
files: one SVG export with text converted to paths

evals.prompt: The film you made last month looks wrong now - I redesigned the board screen and re-exported it. Everything else is the same.
evals.expected_output: Re-runs the existing pipeline rather than rebuilding it, surfaces any layer names that no longer resolve, and either restores them or updates the name map. Does not hard-code around the problem.
files: an existing film project plus a changed SVG export
